analysis.step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram illustrates Levels Beyond's Media to Cloud ingestion and metadata extraction pipeline. Media files uploaded to Amazon S3 trigger an AWS Step Functions workflow. Step Functions initiates parallel actions: (1) triggering AWS Elemental MediaConvert to generate proxy files and write proxy metadata to Amazon DynamoDB, (2) calling Amazon Rekognition to extract visual metadata and timecodes and store them in DynamoDB, and (3) initiating Amazon Transcribe to produce text from audio, which is passed to Amazon Comprehend for entity/profanity analysis before storing the output in DynamoDB. analysis.step_by_step_reasoning: The architecture diagram depicts SundaySky's Rendering as a Service (RAS) platform. Client devices request personalized videos through API Gateway, which invokes a frontend Lambda function. The Lambda pushes rendering instructions to an SQS Jobs Queue and polls an SQS Responses Queue. EC2 Spot Instances in an Auto Scaling Group pick up rendering jobs from the SQS Jobs Queue, upload rendered video segments to an S3 Bucket, and write quick response playlist links back to the SQS Responses Queue, which returns the link to the client. Videos are played back by client devices via CloudFront from S3. Auto scaling is dynamically managed by Step Functions triggering a Scaling Lambda every 15 seconds based on CloudWatch metrics sent by the EC2 instances. Spot instance interruptions are handled via CloudWatch Events triggering an Interruption Handler Lambda, which instructs the EC2 instance to drain remaining jobs and detaches it from the Auto Scaling Group.
